$comment: Misuse and abuse prevention, Standard 9. The shard began in Phase 1 carrying only misuse.safety-controls-not-disabled, the rule the detector detectDisabledSafetyControls binds to. standards/09-misuse-and-abuse-prevention.md states that rule and adds four more, none of which has a detector: three manual-review and one not-evaluable.

rules.title: Provider safety controls are not disabled
rules.description: Configuration does not turn off a model provider's content filtering, moderation or safety settings.
rules.rationale: Disabling a safety control is a decision with a blast radius, and it is almost always made to unblock a test and then never reverted. The setting outlives the reason.
rules.remediation: Restore the provider's default safety configuration, or record why a lower setting is required and what compensates for it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact literal recognition against maintained lists, in the code and string positions of recognised source and configuration file types, and only in a file that also names a recognised safety key; comments are never searched. A spelling, key or file type not on those lists is not seen, and that gap reports as passed, not as not-evaluated: a pass means no recognised disabling literal was found, not that any control is enabled. The rule is withdrawn to not-evaluated only when the walk was shortened by a framework exclusion.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Exemptible, deliberately. Research and red-team systems have a genuine reason to lower a safety setting, and a rule that refused to hear it would be routed around rather than met.

rules.title: Foreseeable misuse is identified, and each case has a named control or a recorded acceptance
rules.description: A committed misuse analysis names, for each foreseeable misuse or abuse case, who could attempt it, the harmful output or effect sought, and the interface it would be attempted through, and records against each case either the control that addresses it or a reasoned acceptance. A provider's default safety setting is named as a control only for a case the analysis shows it addresses. Where no case is identified, the analysis says so and states how that conclusion was reached.
rules.rationale: A system with no written misuse analysis still has misuse cases; they are unexamined, and the first list of them is compiled after an incident. A control with no named case cannot be judged adequate or inadequate, and a case with neither a control nor an acceptance is a gap nobody decided to accept.
rules.remediation: List the foreseeable misuse and abuse cases for the system's users and uses, name the control or the reasoned acceptance for each, and where no case is found, record that finding with the reasoning behind it.

rules.title: Use by any one identity or source is attributed and bounded
rules.description: A system that accepts requests from people or processes outside its operating team attributes each request to an identity or source, bounds the volume of use any one identity or source can obtain, and records the bound and where it is enforced.
rules.rationale: Abuse is often misuse at volume: an output that is tolerable once is harmful ten thousand times, and an unbounded path is the cheapest one to automate. Without attribution, no bound can be applied to anyone in particular.
rules.remediation: Attribute requests to an identity or source, set per-identity or per-source limits suited to the system's declared use, and record the limits and where they are enforced, including when that is deployment configuration outside the repository.

rules.title: Signals of attempted misuse are recorded, reviewed by a named role, and can be acted on
rules.description: Where the misuse analysis names at least one misuse or abuse case, the system records the events by which an attempt would be recognised, names the role that reviews them, and has at least one enforcement action against an identity or source, such as restricting or suspending it, that the reviewer can apply.
rules.rationale: A control that blocks one request does nothing about whoever sends the next. Misuse that is filtered and never reviewed is misuse the operator has arranged not to know about, and a reviewer with no action available can only watch it continue.
rules.remediation: Decide which events indicate attempted misuse, such as filter hits, refusals, limit breaches and reports; record them in a form that meets the pack's rules on logged prompt content; name the reviewing role; and implement at least one enforcement action against an identity or source.

rules.title: Misuse controls prevent or bound the misuse they are named against while the system runs
rules.description: At inference time, the controls the misuse analysis names prevent or bound the misuse cases they are named against.
rules.rationale: A configured filter, a declared limit and a reviewed signal are facts about the repository or the deployment. Whether they stop the misuse they were chosen for is decided by the model, the adversary and the input during a run. It is stated so that the gap is visible in every verdict rather than implied by the presence of controls. It is required rather than forbidden because Standard 9 mints no prohibition.
rules.remediation: Exercise each named control against its misuse case at the current revision and commit the record. Until a rule can read such records this requirement is reported as not evaluated and must not be read as satisfied; even then, a record establishes behaviour only on the inputs it exercised.
rules.$notEvaluableNote: The subject is system behaviour at inference time against a deliberate adversary, not repository content. A human reading the repository can establish which misuse controls are named and configured, which misuse.misuse-cases-identified asks; they cannot establish that those controls stop the misuse they are named against, because that is decided by the model, the adversary's inputs and the running environment. What would make part of it evaluable is a committed record of an adversarial exercise against each named misuse case, from a named harness at a recorded system revision, which a separate rule would check for existence and currency. Even that record establishes behaviour only on the inputs it exercised.
